text:
Elaine: Heads up — saw several 5xxs and p99 cold-starts for hosted models when we scaled-to-zero this morning. p99 ~6–10s on short chat requests. Anyone else seeing the same? thinking about warm-pool sizing vs longer cooldowns.

Mike: Yup, same spike in eu-west1. Telemetry shows CA provisioning ~40s, node ready ~50s, image pull ~20s, model load ~2m. p95 fine, p99 blows up. Posting short trace snippet in thread.

Jia: If model checkpoints are large, warm pool needs nodes with preloaded model cache. Suggest a tiny reserved pool (1 GPU per busy region) + fast prefetch sidecar. Also try lowering scale-down cooldown to 3m for small models.

Sanjay: Lowering cooldown reduces cold starts but increases steady cost. Back-of-envelope: 1 GPU warm in 4 regions ~= $0.45/hr * 4 = ~$1.8/hr. Need cost/latency tradeoff.

Elaine: Can we break cold-start into buckets? Node boot, kubelet, image pull, model load. My traces: node creation 35s, kubelet ready 50s, image pull 20s, model load 120s. Model load is dominant.

Mike: Agreed model load kills us. Options: snapshot KV cache to S3 and async restore, mmap checkpoints, or keep libcaches warm. Also shorter image layers helps.

Jia: Another pattern: keep nodes scaled to small (scale pods to 0 but nodes remain warm) via a dedicated warm node pool with taint:NoSchedule + tolerations for prewarm jobs. When needed, remove taint. Reuse nodes via cordon/drain scripts instead of creating new ones.

Sanjay: Watch out for preemptible/spot instances as warm pool — preempts trigger extra cold starts. For regions with >2 preempts/hr, use on-demand warm nodes.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] 1765002000 model-serving-spot-eviction in ap-southeast1 - 3 preempts in last hour.

Elaine: That's the ap-southeast noise. Proposal: warm-pool=on-demand for ap-southeast1 and eu-west1 for now. Others can be spot-backed.

Mike: We can label nodepools and teach CA to prefer them. Example CA snippet: 
```
clusterAutoscaler:
  expander: least-waste
  scaleDownDelayAfterAdd: 10m
  scaleDownUnneededTime: 15m
```
Also we can set nodePool annotation warm-pool=true.

Sanjay: Also consider predictive scaling: use request-rate + queue-depth metric to pre-scale 60s out. We have a small ML predictor with ~85% accuracy for ramp-ups. If accurate, it avoids a lot of cold starts without big warm cost.

Jia: Agreed. Plus tune cooldowns per model: tiny models get short cooldowns, big LLMs longer + prefetch. For prefetch, run a background job that pulls and memory-maps the checkpoint.

Elaine: Quick ops decision for today? 1) Create 1 GPU on-demand warm pool in eu-west1 and ap-southeast1. 2) Enable async prefetch for top-10 models. 3) Ship predictive-scaler prototype (60s lookahead) for 2 weeks. 4) Measure p99 and cost delta. Who owns?

Mike: I'll own the predictive-scaler prototype.

Sanjay: I'll size warm pools and do pricing calc + preemptibility analysis.

Jia: I'll implement async prefetch + docker layer slim-down.

Elaine: I'll update runbook, add alert threshold: p99 latency > 3s for 15m triggers page to oncall and creates a ticket. Also add note: prefer on-demand warm nodes in regions with >2 preempts/hr.

Mike: Quick commands I'll add to repo:
```
# cordon candidate node
kubectl cordon gpu-warm-01
# drain carefully (ignore daemonsets, wait for grace periods)
kubectl drain gpu-warm-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

Sanjay: I'll also add a small script to snapshot checkpoint metadata to S3 so prefetch can pick it up faster.

oncall-bot: Noted. Alert policy updated: p99_model_latency > 3s for 15m -> page.

Elaine: Thanks all. We'll reconvene in 2 weeks to review p99 and cost. :thumbsup:
